scientific_question: Can independent cultivated-plant occurrence records document anthropogenic butterfly host exposure in Florida outside the naturalized/wild WCVP distribution, even where native/introduced plant range reconstruction contains no host opportunity?

taxa.selection_rationale: Cultivated exotic Phoebis larval host with local adult emergence documented by Koptur et al. (2024), but no frozen WCVP FLA record

iNaturalist_observations.sampling: Retrieve total_results for each status, and only up to 100 top public observations for source audit; do not treat sample counts as the total
iNaturalist_observations.rates: no comparison of cultivated vs wild proportions as real abundance because reporting, tagging and ascertainment differ
iNaturalist_observations.source_requires: source URL, taxon exact species (or infra under it), captive true, date, photo, public location and accuracy

pilot_gate: A source-confirmed positive for Senna polyphylla requires at least 3 explicitly captive/cultivated, photo-supported, <=1000 m positional accuracy observations within Florida in at least two approximately 5 km cells; call this a cultivated occurrence footprint outside frozen WCVP distribution, not butterfly utilization or horticultural extent.
failure: If data are absent/ambiguous, retain Koptur (2024) only as the independent cultivation and larval-emergence example. Do not broaden to an invented global effect.
boundaries: iNaturalist cultivated annotations may be incomplete or erroneous; absence of records is not absence of garden plants
Photos are not externally adjudicated cultivated evidence without field or image review
Plant occurrence does NOT document butterfly feeding, reproduction, colonization, or fitness at that particular observation
Do not treat WCVP no Florida range record as proof there are no established populations
Floristic and invertebrate observation metadata have drastically different detection effort
